summary: The schema-5 candidate model predicts a FRAME-LEVEL outcome, not a per-candidate ranking. Because every candidate row of a planning frame shares the same heldGain/lossRisk label, the model regresses to a near-constant per-frame value. Its cross-candidate score spread is therefore tiny; at control gain 18 the additive utility shift (~2.1) is smaller than the rule-utility gaps (5-15), so the neural channel almost never re-orders the candidates. Result: the candidate arm's endLand is byte-identical to the rule-basis in all 72 prior engine matches.

rootCauseChain.evidence: trainer/v5-labels.cjs buildLabels(): heldGain = clamp01((land[j]-land[i])/landScale) and lossRisk = clamp01(maxDrop/landScale) are computed from visibleState.land over the window [t, t+horizonTicks] and assigned to the frame. frameRows() in tools/benchmark/v5-dataset.cjs expands each planning frame to one ROW per candidate, but every candidate row of that frame is stamped with the SAME label. Only the chosen+executed candidate is observed:true; unchosen candidates are counterfactual (null).
rootCauseChain.implication: The supervised target does not distinguish candidates within a frame. The model is a frame-value predictor, not a candidate ranker.

rootCauseChain.claim: The trained model therefore emits near-constant per-candidate scores.
rootCauseChain.evidence: trainer/v5-control-evidence.cjs (fresh run this session): candidate-v5-v2 (lr0.1-e300) meanCrossCandidateScoreStd = 0.1159, decisionDepartures = 7/1034; lr0.2-e200 meanCrossCandidateScoreStd = 0.1206, decisionDepartures = 4/1034. evaluationDepartureRate = 0.8598 (the model's SHADOW ranking differs from the rule on 85.98% of frames) but the bounded control arm changes the actual pick on only 7/1034 frames. Sampled per-kind scores are near-constant: hold 0.649, invest 0.649, attack 0.614, naval 0.817.
rootCauseChain.implication: The score DOES carry a weak discriminative signal in shadow mode (85.98% shadow departure), but its absolute spread across candidates in a frame is ~0.116.

rootCauseChain.claim: Gain-18 control is too small to re-order the rule utilities.
rootCauseChain.evidence: src/runtime/decision-kernels.cjs candidateControlKernel: utility = round(utility + g*score), g = clamp(gain,0,60), default gain 18. Max cross-candidate shift ~= 0.116 * 18 ~= 2.1. Rule utilities in trainer/v5-control-evidence.cjs buildCandidateSet span 35-125 with gaps typically >=5-15. So the neural term rarely crosses a rule-utility boundary.
rootCauseChain.implication: The signal is present in scoring but not carried into the decision at gain 18.

rootCauseChain.claim: Net effect: candidate endLand is exactly equal to rule-basis.
rootCauseChain.evidence: docs/campaign-openfront-neural-v5v2-20260924.md section 3: across 1v1, official-2v2 and ffa-duo (24 matches each, 72 total) the candidate arm's endLand is IDENTICAL to the rule-basis in every scenario (paired land mean diff 0.0, CI [0,0]).
rootCauseChain.implication: The gain-18 schema-5 control is empirically non-binding on this dataset.

dataImbalance.implication: The model barely sees aggressive/expansion actions and never a confirmed win, so it cannot learn the value of the decisions that actually change matches.

lossRiskCalibration.implication: lossRisk is over-predicted in the mid bin, inflating the subtracted risk term and further compressing the effective score spread (trainer/campaign-20260924/calibration.json).

mapsToMandateCauses.missingCandidateFeatures: NOT the primary cause (candidate-specific features ARE present and fed at runtime; featuredSchemaVersion 2 = 32 active / 0 constant)
mapsToMandateCauses.staleOrConstantFeatures: NOT the cause (feature parity verified 32 active / 0 constant)
mapsToMandateCauses.shadowOnlyInference: PARTIAL (shadow ranking IS discriminative at 85.98%, but the bounded control does not use it)
mapsToMandateCauses.ruleOverride: NOT the cause (the model never re-orders, so the rule stands)
mapsToMandateCauses.datasetMeanLearning: CONFIRMED (MSE to a frame-level target drives regression toward the frame value)

decisiveBottleneck: The training objective (frame-level MSE) does not reward cross-candidate discrimination, so the model's per-candidate score spread (~0.116) is too small for gain-18 control to re-order rule utilities. The fix is a candidate-group RANKING objective (chosen candidate must rank above unchosen ones within the same frame) combined with outcome calibration, plus a data curriculum that supplies the under-represented action kinds and confirmed outcomes.

proposedFix.learning: Add a within-frame pairwise/listwise ranking loss (chosen candidate score > unchosen candidate scores) on top of the outcome-regression term, so the score is both calibrated and discriminative.
proposedFix.data: Targeted real-match curriculum (military/expansion, economy/defense, marine, team/duo, hard opponents) via tools/benchmark/v5-dataset.cjs, with the action-type distribution as an explicit quality gate.
proposedFix.runtime: Keep the gain-18 candidateControlKernel; with a discriminative score the shift should become binding without changing the runtime architecture.
proposedFix.compat: Optionally extend candidate-policy-v5.validate() to accept a versioned 32x40x2 arch (1402 weights) which had the best offline valMSE, for an architecture comparison on the new objective.
